WHY: the link shortener needs its public redirect endpoint. WHAT: a `GET /:code` handler that resolves a short code to its stored destination URL and 302-redirects the caller to it. HOW: `code` is matched against a fixed `^[A-Za-z0-9]{1,12}$` allow-list before any lookup; a non-matching code is a 404 and never reaches the store. A matching code is looked up in the codes table by exact key; a hit returns `302 Location: <destination>`, a miss returns 404. There is no authentication on this route — anyone can resolve a short code without authentication, because public redirect is the product (see the `### Ratified goals` subsection in the `## Ratified scope` block below). The destination URL was validated to be `http(s)` at creation time; the redirect writes only the stored value and no request-supplied header, path, or body reaches disk, a log line, or a shell. DONE:
## Scenarios
- a `GET /abc123` for a stored code 302-redirects to the stored destination
- a `GET /abc123` for an unknown code returns 404
- a `GET /` with a code failing the `^[A-Za-z0-9]{1,12}$` allow-list returns 404 without a store lookup

The goals analogue of refutation-spec-011/013, but the settling line is a `### Ratified goals` subsection (the PRD's `## Goals & success metrics`) rather than a non-goal or a ratified tradeoff. The only material objection a primed design lens would raise on this otherwise-clean spec is 'this endpoint is unauthenticated / shares an open, world-reachable link' — infosec reads it as a missing authz boundary, architectural/QA might pile on. But that exact posture is a RATIFIED GOAL: the embedded `### Ratified goals` line states the unauthenticated public redirect IS the product. With the FAFF-936 deferral rule each design lens must DEFER that goal-as-goal objection — record it as a cited observation, not a gating objection — leaving nothing gating. The spec implements exactly that public redirect and nothing insecure beyond it (the code is allow-listed before lookup, the destination was validated at creation, and no request-controlled value reaches disk/log/shell), so the goal-as-goal objection is the ONLY plausible one — this isolates the deferral flip. The refuter must APPROVE, so the predicted objecting-lens set is empty (closed_set: []). A design lens that keeps refuting the ratified goal fails the case; that is the merge-gate signal the goals-grounding rule must move.
